title: Open on the question the text answers
statement: Build a pre-reading opening around the question the text will answer: pose it early, give the knowledge the reading needs, and close on it to send students into the text.
example: One opening named four pieces of knowledge the reading needs: the world, the people, the kind of story and the words to write about it.
detail: The handover's eight-scene opening for a play ends by returning to the central transformation and leading into the first scene, and the narration handoff asks that the final question invite the learner into the reading. The recorded script sets the unit's job in its first scene, to trace how the hero gets from one state to the other, names four pieces of knowledge the reading needs (the world of the play, the people in it, the kind of story it is and the words to write about it), and closes by telling students to open the book. The film treatment's last scene returns to the opening question before the play's first scene.
against: How much of that knowledge belongs before the reading is disputed: in the film study, "Only 6 are needed before the play's first line: the setting and who is who, 35 seconds of narration." (othello-unit-video/research/FINDINGS.md, lines 87-88), while another 11 of its 26 points could go in at the line that first needs them.

evidence.quote: Your job, across this whole unit, is to trace how a man gets from one to the other. From A to B.
To see how, you need four pieces of knowledge: the world of the play, the people in it, the kind of story it is, and the words you will use to write about it. Knowledge first. Then the reading.
A man who loves his wife. A man who hates him. Five acts between them. Now you know the world. Open the book.
Start with place, then intimacy, then the tragic reversal. Let the final question invite the learner into the reading.
8. Begin with Iago. Return to the central transformation and lead into reading Act 1 Scene 1.
Return to the opening question before Act 1, Scene 1.
